explainBack.question: Why doesn't the new Windows Age API automatically make every app on a child's PC safer today?
explainBack.answer: Because three separate steps must each happen: the API is only running on Windows Insider preview builds, not general Windows; even where it runs, it only passes an age category or verification status from the account to an app; and the app's developer must then choose to request that signal and decide what experience follows. Until a developer acts on the signal, nothing in the app changes — and existing protections like screen-time requests still travel through Family Safety, a different path entirely.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: P004 states the APIs are Insider-only and not a universal age check; P006 states the developer decides what follows from the signal and that Family Safety remains the separate control path.
explainBack.assessment: The article supports this causal answer completely in ordinary language; every step of the chain is explicit in P004 and P006, so a reader can reconstruct it without outside knowledge.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A parent sees a game studio announce that its popular PC game 'now supports Windows age signals,' and assumes this means the game will now enforce their child's two-hour daily screen-time limit.
unseenTransfer.question: Using only the article's mechanism, what will and won't change for this family?
unseenTransfer.answer: The announcement means the game's developer chose to read the age category the Microsoft account can supply — say '10–12' — and may adjust its own content or features accordingly. It will not enforce screen-time limits: those live in the Family Safety layer, and a request for more time still goes through the Family Safety app. Also, unless the family's PC runs an Insider build or the API has since reached general Windows, the signal may not even be available yet; the parent should check general availability rather than assume it.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: P006 (developer decides what follows from the signal; screen time still goes through Family Safety), P004 (Insider-only, not universal), P009 (ask which layer a claim describes).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's three-layer model resolves this novel scenario cleanly and prevents the exact misreading it warns against, confirming genuine transfer rather than headline recall.
